snippet.title: Imlac PDS-1 game: FREEWAY CROSSING PROGRAM (1971)
snippet.description:
This is the Freeway Crossing game from 1971, running on an Imlac PDS-1 emulator.  The game was supposedly used in psychology experiments at University of Washington.  It may or may not have been an inspiration for the Frogger arcade game.  Emulation was a bit of a challenge due to the game being written for an early "Alpha" model, as opposed to the later "Graphics" model.  No documentation has been found for the former.  Zachary Harper reverse engineered the details from the game listing.

The game was written in 1971 by Michael Irrgang at the University of Washington.  It was written as part of an experiment in reaction times conducted by psychology professor Earl Hunt.
